quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Either the caretaker or the assistant ___ responsible for locking up.
quests.completedSentence: Either the caretaker or the assistant is responsible for locking up.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: In 'either...or' sentences, the verb agrees with the noun nearest to it - here, 'the assistant', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: With 'either...or', check the noun that's closest to the blank.
quests.example: Either the caretaker or the assistant is responsible for locking up.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Either my brother or my sister ___ picking me up from the airport.
quests.completedSentence: Either my brother or my sister is picking me up from the airport.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'my sister', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Look at the second name in the pair, not the first, to decide the verb.
quests.example: Either my brother or my sister is picking me up from the airport.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Either the printer or the scanner ___ broken.
quests.completedSentence: Either the printer or the scanner is broken.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the scanner', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The noun right before the verb is what matters in an 'either...or' sentence.
quests.example: Either the printer or the scanner is broken.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even when the two nouns differ in number
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Either the manager or the employees ___ responsible for this decision.
quests.completedSentence: Either the manager or the employees are responsible for this decision.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even when the two nouns differ in number
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the employees', which is plural, so the verb is 'are', even though 'the manager' (singular) comes first.
quests.nativeTip: This time, the second option is plural - see how that changes the verb.
quests.example: Either the manager or the employees are responsible for this decision.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even when the two nouns differ in number
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Either the students or the teacher ___ mistaken about the schedule.

quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the teacher', which is singular, so the verb is 'is', even though 'the students' (plural) comes first.
quests.nativeTip: Compare this to the last question - here the second option is singular instead.
quests.example: Either the students or the teacher is mistaken about the schedule.

quests.nativeTip: Focus on 'the player', not 'the coaches', since it's the noun right before the verb.

quests.completedSentence: Not only the recipe but also the cooking method is important for this dish.
quests.grammarRule: 'Not only...but also' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the cooking method', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Check the second item in the pair, since it's the one right before the verb.
quests.example: Not only the recipe but also the cooking method is important for this dish.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The editor, as well as her assistants, ___ attending the conference.
quests.completedSentence: The editor, as well as her assistants, is attending the conference.
quests.grammarRule: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'the editor', which is singular; 'as well as her assistants' is just added detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'As well as' just adds extra information - it doesn't create a true compound subject like 'and' does.
quests.example: The editor, as well as her assistants, is attending the conference.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The students, as well as their teacher, ___ excited about the field trip.
quests.completedSentence: The students, as well as their teacher, are excited about the field trip.
quests.grammarRule: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'the students', which is plural. The verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase after 'as well as' doesn't change how many students there are.
quests.example: The students, as well as their teacher, are excited about the field trip.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: This recipe, as well as several others in the book, ___ easy to follow.
quests.completedSentence: This recipe, as well as several others in the book, is easy to follow.
quests.grammarRule: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'this recipe', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Focus on the original subject before the comma, not the phrase after 'as well as'.
quests.example: This recipe, as well as several others in the book, is easy to follow.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The CEO, together with several board members, ___ reviewing the proposal.
quests.completedSentence: The CEO, together with several board members, is reviewing the proposal.
quests.grammarRule: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'the CEO', which is singular; 'together with several board members' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Together with' works just like 'as well as' - it doesn't add a second subject.
quests.example: The CEO, together with several board members, is reviewing the proposal.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The players, along with their coach, ___ heading to the airport tonight.

quests.grammarRule: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'the players', which is plural. The verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Along with' behaves the same way - check the original subject before the comma.
quests.example: The players, along with their coach, are heading to the airport tonight.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject

quests.grammarRule: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'this document', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The attachments mentioned after 'together with' don't change the number of the main subject.
quests.example: This document, together with several attachments, is ready to be sent.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Accompanied by' / 'including' do not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The bride, accompanied by her parents, ___ into the ceremony hall.

quests.grammarRule: 'Accompanied by' / 'including' do not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'the bride', which is singular; 'accompanied by her parents' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'walks'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Accompanied by' introduces extra detail, just like 'as well as' and 'together with'.
quests.example: The bride, accompanied by her parents, walks into the ceremony hall.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Accompanied by' / 'including' do not change the number of the original subject

quests.grammarRule: 'Accompanied by' / 'including' do not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'the whole family', a singular collective noun; 'including the grandparents' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Including' works the same way - the original subject decides the verb.
quests.example: The whole family, including the grandparents, is attending the reunion this year.
